Speaking to reporters in Florida, Trump described the operation as minor and said the targeted equipment had been destroyed. Iranian state media reported two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, near the strategic Strait of Hormuz.  Trump has repeatedly portrayed military and economic pressure as forcing Tehran toward an agreement. In earlier remarks in September, he called the U.S. naval blockade the “greatest blockade ever in military history” and claimed Iran wanted a deal because its revenues were being squeezed. Those descriptions represent the president’s assessment.  However, Iranian officials have presented a more guarded picture. A senior official told Reuters this week that the sides remained far apart, with Tehran demanding an end to the blockade, relief from oil sanctions and access to frozen funds.  Qatar is continuing mediation, with Iran reviewing proposals intended to bridge differences over its nuclear program. No final agreement has been announced.
